newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary meat firm's output stable despite strike.
newsitem.headline: Hungary meat firm's output stable despite strike.

text.p: A strike by employees of Hungary's second-biggest pork processor, Szekszardi Husipari Rt, did not disrupt production on Monday, the firm's chief executive said.

"We had regular output during the night, morning and afternoon shifts today," Adam Tamas told Reuters in a telephone interview from this south-central Hungarian town. "We expect to complete ... the production we scheduled for today."

Several hundred demonstrators, including SzHRt employees, held a protest in front of the Parliament building in Budapest Monday afternoon, demanding higher pay raises than the 15 percent offered by SzHRt.
Tamas said that altogether slightly more than 100 of SzHRt's 1,100 employees failed to turn up to work during the three shifts today.
SzHRt processes between 300,000 and 350,000 pigs a year, some 20 percent of the country's total, as well as between 20,000 and 25,000 cattle and other livestock, Tamas said.
He said that much of the production is exported, adding that only Pick Rt has a larger turnover from livestock processing than SzHRt.
SzHRt's majority owner is Germany's Metraco, which in turn is controlled by German investor Gunther Schlegel.
